---
title: "Episode Leadership Across Seasons"
subtitle: "EXPLORE THE DIALOGUE SEASON BY SEASON"
format: html
---

The other episode comparison groups seasons 1-7 and 15-21. Here, each season is shown separately to make changes over time easier to explore. An episode is kid-led when the four boys have more lines, adult-led when the six selected adults have more, and a tie when their recorded line counts are equal.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(southparkr)
library(plotly)

core_boys <- c("Stan", "Kyle", "Cartman", "Kenny")
selected_adults <- c("Randy", "Mr. Garrison", "Chef", "Gerald", "Sharon", "Mr. Mackey")

dialogue_lines <- episode_lines |>
  mutate(character = str_remove_all(character, "[:\"]"))

episode_catalog <- dialogue_lines |>
  distinct(season_number, season_episode_number, episode_name)

episode_cast_counts <- dialogue_lines |>
  filter(character %in% c(core_boys, selected_adults)) |>
  mutate(cast = if_else(character %in% core_boys, "kids", "adults")) |>
  count(season_number, season_episode_number, episode_name, cast, name = "lines") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = cast, values_from = lines, values_fill = 0)

episode_leadership <- episode_catalog |>
  left_join(
    episode_cast_counts,
    by = c("season_number", "season_episode_number", "episode_name")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    across(c(kids, adults), \(x) replace_na(x, 0L)),
    leadership = case_when(
      adults > kids ~ "Adult-led",
      kids > adults ~ "Kid-led",
      TRUE ~ "Tie"
    )
  )

leadership_by_season <- episode_leadership |>
  count(season_number, leadership, name = "episodes") |>
  complete(
    season_number = sort(unique(episode_leadership$season_number)),
    leadership = c("Kid-led", "Adult-led", "Tie"),
    fill = list(episodes = 0)
  ) |>
  group_by(season_number) |>
  mutate(
    total_episodes = sum(episodes),
    share = 100 * episodes / total_episodes,
    leadership = factor(leadership, levels = c("Kid-led", "Adult-led", "Tie"))
  ) |>
  ungroup()

season_leadership_plot <- leadership_by_season |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = season_number,
    y = share,
    color = leadership,
    group = leadership,
    text = paste(
      "Season:", season_number,
      "<br>Dialogue leader:", leadership,
      "<br>Episodes:", episodes, "of", total_episodes,
      "<br>Share:", round(share, 1), "%"
    )
  )) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(leadership_by_season$season_number))) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Kid-led" = "#005A9C", "Adult-led" = "#A33A13", "Tie" = "#4F5B5E")) +
  labs(
    title = "Episode dialogue leadership by season",
    x = "Season",
    y = "Share of episodes",
    color = "Dialogue leader",
    caption = "Source: southparkr transcript data"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(season_leadership_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
season_leadership_table <- leadership_by_season |>
  select(season_number, total_episodes, leadership, episodes, share) |>
  mutate(share = round(share, 1)) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = leadership,
    values_from = c(episodes, share)
  )

knitr::kable(
  season_leadership_table,
  caption = "Episode counts and shares by season"
)
```

Use the chart's hover labels to see the episode counts behind each point. A high adult-led share means more episodes in that season have more dialogue from the selected adults; it does not establish that the adults drive the plot.
